# Analytical Skills for Business (01/2026) {-}


\BQ

\question{} **Version Control Systems: Git and GitHub**
\BP
\part[6]{} Explain the key differences between Git and GitHub. What is the primary purpose of each?
\part[6]{} Describe three core concepts in Git—repository, commit, and branch—and explain their importance in collaborative analytics projects.
<!-- \part[5]{} Explain the difference between merging and rebasing in Git. When would you use one approach over the other? -->
\EP

\question{} **Programming Languages and Development Environments**
\BP
\part[6]{} Compare Python and SQL in terms of their primary use cases in business analytics.
\part[9]{} Explain three key elements of programming languages (choose from syntax, libraries, variables, functions, objects, conditions, loops) and describe why each is important for data analysis.
\part[6]{} Define what containers like Docker do in software development and data analytics. Explain the main benefits they provide.
\part[6]{} Explain the concept of an IDE and name two popular IDEs used for data analytics.
\EP

\question{}**No-Code and Low-Code Tools**
\BP
\part[9]{} Name and describe three no-code or low-code tools for data analytics covered in the course (choose from n8n, Snowflake, QGIS, Tableau, Power BI, KNIME).
\part[8]{} Explain the advantages of using no-code/low-code tools in business analytics and discuss situations where these tools might be preferred over traditional programming methods.
\EP

\question{} **Statistics and Analytics**
\BP
\part[9]{} Explain three measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and when each is most appropriate to use.
\part[9]{} Distinguish between univariate, bivariate, and multivariate data analysis. Provide one business example for each.
\part[6]{} Describe three common data quality issues (from: missing values, inconsistent data, duplicate records, outliers) and appropriate strategies for handling each.
<!-- \part[6]{} Explain the difference between correlation and regression analysis. Why is it important to remember that "correlation does not imply causation"? -->
\EP
